hero_eyebrow: An AI reading companion for macOS and Windows
hero_title: Understand what you read, one passage at a time.
hero_body: Open a supported document, select a passage, and ask an AI model about it. Your library stays on your computer. Questions, conversation history, document metadata and selected text go to your chosen provider; without a selection, an outline and opening excerpt are included.
hero_visual_alt: Illustration: a document in the Library, a highlighted passage in the reader, and an answer with a citation chip.
values_title: Read, ask, and check the source
values_body: Three things VStudy Pro does, and does carefully.
value_1_body: PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, HTML, CSV, Markdown and plain text become clean Markdown. PDFs go through our own parser first, with MarkItDown as a fallback. Your original file is kept alongside.
value_2_title: Ask about exactly what you selected
value_2_body: Select a passage, or use a whole section, and ask in your own words. The model is instructed to use that text and to say when it does not support an answer.
value_3_body: When the model cites a section or page, click the citation to jump there and check it yourself.
demo_title: See how a question becomes a conversation
demo_body: A scripted example using the sample document. No model is called.
demo_step_3: Get an answer grounded in that text
demo_step_4: Follow the citation back to the source
demo_steps_label: How it works, in four steps
demo_answer: Answer a question from memory tomorrow, then again next week.
demo_swap_hint: Prefer the chat on the other side? Swap it from the toolbar.
who_title: Made for people who read to learn
who_body: Four people, four kinds of documents, one way of working.
p1_situation: Midterms next week: lecture PDFs, a long PowerPoint deck, and notes in Chinese, Japanese and English.
p1_job: Read slides as text and ask for an explanation in your preferred language.
p1_first: Select a slide's text and ask "Explain this simply." Set Reply language in Settings.
p2_situation: Working through a stack of papers for a literature review, and needing to check what a results table actually reports.
p2_job: Read papers and ruled tables, then check any cited sections or pages.
p2_first: Citations that jump to the page, and one folder per project.
p3_situation: Before Thursday's meeting: a supplier contract in Word, a quarterly report as a PDF, and the spreadsheet behind it.
p3_job: Ask about a clause or figure and check cited evidence before relying on it.
p3_first: "Use this section" to ask about a whole clause. Excel sheets read as tables.
p4_situation: Reading a bilingual article, one language per line, and wondering why a phrase is used the way it is.
p4_job: Keep the original and ask about grammar, nuance and word choice in your reply language.
p4_first: Pick a Reply language, then select a single sentence and ask about it.

models_note: VStudy Pro finds installed CLIs without launching them. After you enable a provider, opening the model picker or refreshing Settings checks its models. Saved API keys use macOS Keychain encryption on Mac or DPAPI on Windows. CLI models get no tools: they see only the text VStudy Pro sends.

data_private_2: Saved API keys use OS encryption (Mac Keychain or Windows DPAPI); session keys stay in memory

good_to_know: VStudy Pro is a macOS and Windows app. It reads the text layer of PDFs and has no OCR yet, so scanned pages can't be read. Word, Excel and PowerPoint means .docx, .xlsx and .pptx, up to 50 MB per file. It doesn't sync between devices and isn't a note-taking app. The first conversion needs internet once to set up the converter. The first conversion asks to download packages from PyPI and possibly Python from GitHub. Choose Offline to read Markdown and text; retry conversion when ready.
start_body: Pick something you actually need to understand this week.
hero_excerpt: Explain one idea in your own words, then return to it later.
hero_answer: Answer a question from memory tomorrow, then again next week.
demo_selection: A useful habit is to explain one idea in your own words.
try_steps: Import the sample, then wait until its pages are ready. Select a sentence by dragging across it, type “Explain this sentence” in Chat, choose a model and send. Open a numbered citation and compare its source with the answer. AI setup may be needed before sending.
citation_hint: Open a citation number to read the source and check whether it supports the answer.
